questions.text:
Consider the system of linear equations given below.

[latex] \begin{array}{c} a x+y=b \\ 16 x+a y=24 \end{array} [/latex]

Suppose the values of [latex]a[/latex] and [latex]b[/latex] are chosen such that the system of linear equations produce multiple solutions. Then the product of [latex]a[/latex] and [latex]b[/latex] is ________. (answer in integer)
questions.solution:
The system [latex]ax+y=b,\ 16x+ay=24[/latex] has infinitely many (multiple) solutions exactly when the two equations describe the same line, i.e. all three coefficient ratios are equal:
[latex]\dfrac{a}{16}=\dfrac{1}{a}=\dfrac{b}{24}[/latex]

From [latex]\dfrac{a}{16}=\dfrac{1}{a}[/latex]: [latex]a^2=16\Rightarrow a=\pm4[/latex].
From [latex]\dfrac{1}{a}=\dfrac{b}{24}[/latex]: [latex]b=\dfrac{24}{a}[/latex].

If [latex]a=4[/latex]: [latex]b=24/4=6[/latex], so [latex]ab=4\times6=24[/latex].
If [latex]a=-4[/latex]: [latex]b=24/(-4)=-6[/latex], so [latex]ab=(-4)\times(-6)=24[/latex].

Either valid choice of [latex]a[/latex] gives the same product.

Answer: 24

questions.text:
Consider an array [latex]A=[10,7,8,19,41,35,25,31][/latex]. Suppose the merge sort algorithm is executed on array [latex]A[/latex] to sort it in increasing order. The merge sort algorithm will carry out a total of [latex]7[/latex] merge operations.

A merge operation on sorted left array [latex]L[/latex] and sorted right array [latex]R[/latex] is said to be void if the output of the merge operation is the elements of array [latex]L[/latex] followed by the elements of array [latex]R[/latex].

The number of void merge operations among these [latex]7[/latex] merge operations is ________. (answer in integer)
questions.solution:
A merge is void when every element of the left sub-array is already [latex]\le[/latex] every element of the right sub-array, so the merge simply concatenates them with no interleaving.

Trace merge sort on [latex]A=[10,7,8,19,41,35,25,31][/latex]:

Bottom level (pairs):
[latex][10],[7]\to[7,10][/latex] (result is [latex]R[/latex] then [latex]L[/latex], not "[latex]L[/latex] then [latex]R[/latex]") — not void.
[latex][8],[19]\to[8,19][/latex] (already [latex]L[/latex] then [latex]R[/latex] as-is) — void.
[latex][41],[35]\to[35,41][/latex] — not void.
[latex][25],[31]\to[25,31][/latex] (already in order) — void.

Next level (quads):
[latex][7,10]+[8,19]\to[7,8,10,19][/latex] (interleaved, not simply [latex]L[/latex] then [latex]R[/latex]) — not void.
[latex][35,41]+[25,31]\to[25,31,35,41][/latex] (interleaved) — not void.

Final merge:
[latex][7,8,10,19]+[25,31,35,41][/latex]: every element of the left ([latex]\le19[/latex]) is already smaller than every element of the right ([latex]\ge25[/latex]), so the merge is simply [latex]L[/latex] followed by [latex]R[/latex] — void.

Total merges [latex]=4+2+1=7[/latex] (matches the given count), with exactly [latex]3[/latex] of them void.

Answer: 3

questions.text: If an IP network uses a subnet mask of [latex]255.255.240.0[/latex], the maximum number of IP addresses that can be assigned to network interfaces is ________. (answer in integer)
questions.solution:
Subnet mask [latex]255.255.240.0[/latex] in binary: [latex]11111111.11111111.11110000.00000000[/latex] — this has [latex]20[/latex] network bits (a [latex]/20[/latex]).

Host bits [latex]=32-20=12[/latex], giving [latex]2^{12}=4096[/latex] total addresses in the subnet. Of these, [latex]2[/latex] are reserved (the all-zeros network address and the all-ones broadcast address) and cannot be assigned to interfaces.

Usable addresses [latex]=4096-2=4094[/latex].

Answer: 4094

questions.text: The [latex]32[/latex]-bit [latex]\text{IEEE}[/latex] [latex]754[/latex] single precision representation of a number is [latex]0\text{xC}2710000[/latex]. The number in decimal representation is ________. (rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
Decode [latex]0\text{xC2710000}[/latex] as IEEE-754 single precision:

Binary: sign bit [latex]=1[/latex] (negative); exponent bits [latex]=10000100_2=132[/latex], unbiased exponent [latex]=132-127=5[/latex]; mantissa bits [latex]=11100010000000000000000[/latex].

Mantissa value [latex]=1+2^{-1}+2^{-2}+2^{-3}+2^{-7}=1+0.5+0.25+0.125+0.0078125=1.8828125[/latex].

Value [latex]=-1.8828125\times2^{5}=-1.8828125\times32=-60.25[/latex].

Answer: -60.25

questions.text:
A lexical analyzer uses the following token definitions

[latex]{letter → [A-Za-z]}[/latex]
[latex]{digit → [0-9]}[/latex]
[latex]{id → letter (letter | digit)^*}[/latex]
[latex]{number → digit}[/latex] [latex]{ }^{+}[/latex]
[latex]{ws → (blank | tab| newline)}[/latex] [latex]{ }^{+}[/latex]

For the string given below,

[latex] x1 \quad 23 {~mm} \quad 78 \quad \text{ y } \quad 7 z \quad \text { zz5 } \quad 14 A \quad 8 H \quad \text { AaYcD } [/latex]

the number of tokens (excluding ws) that will be produced by the lexical analyzer is ________. (answer in integer)
questions.solution:
Tokenize using maximal munch (the longest possible match at each point), skipping whitespace-separated groups: [latex]\text{x1}\ \ \text{23mm}\ \ \text{78}\ \ \text{y}\ \ \text{7z}\ \ \text{zz5}\ \ \text{14A}\ \ \text{8H}\ \ \text{AaYcD}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{array}{l|l}\text{Group}&\text{Tokens produced}\\\hline\text{x1}&\text{id("x1")}\ (1)\\\text{23mm}&\text{number("23"), id("mm")}\ (2)\\\text{78}&\text{number("78")}\ (1)\\\text{y}&\text{id("y")}\ (1)\\\text{7z}&\text{number("7"), id("z")}\ (2)\\\text{zz5}&\text{id("zz5")}\ (1)\ [\text{letter then letter/digit}^*\text{ swallows the trailing digit}]\\\text{14A}&\text{number("14"), id("A")}\ (2)\\\text{8H}&\text{number("8"), id("H")}\ (2)\\\text{AaYcD}&\text{id("AaYcD")}\ (1)\end{array}[/latex]

Total tokens [latex]=1+2+1+1+2+1+2+2+1=13[/latex].

Answer: 13
